executive_summary: QF-20260911-878 shipped lib/fleet/model-policy.cjs (worker seats pinned to claude-opus-5, role seats to claude-fable-5-1 at spawn) but deliberately deferred wiring a mismatch signal into the live SessionStart hook and a fleet-dashboard off-policy count, since both touch critical-path/shared infrastructure. LEAD-phase validation-agent, risk-agent, and prospective testing-agent evidence all independently measured that the naive wiring (feeding scripts/hooks/capture-session-id.cjs's observed role directly through model-policy.cjs's seatClassFor) produces reproducible false positives -- including on the live coordinator seat and on every role seat's first-ever SessionStart, since role/is_coordinator metadata is written by separate registration steps AFTER the generic SessionStart hook runs. This PRD delivers a corrected, fail-open signal built on lib/fleet/role-status-identity.cjs's existing three-state (role/worker/unknown) classifier, using the hook's own pre-write metadata snapshot rather than a fresh classification, plus an independent fleet-dashboard off-policy count, plus CI-visible test coverage (the naive plan would have added tests to *.test.cjs files vitest's CI config never collects).

functional_requirements.title: SessionStart model-policy mismatch signal
functional_requirements.description: In scripts/hooks/capture-session-id.cjs, export a new function signalModelPolicyMismatch({ existingMetadata, model, supabase, emit, now }) with injected deps (emit defaults to lib/governance/emit-feedback.js's emitFeedback; supabase/now injectable for tests). Classification MUST use the hook's own PRE-write existingMetadata object (already fetched before its upsert -- the exact object buildSessionMetadata(existingMetadata, ...) already receives) run through lib/fleet/role-status-identity.cjs's verdictFromMetadata -- NEVER lib/fleet/model-policy.cjs's seatClassFor directly, which collapses an absent/unknown role to 'worker' and false-positives both on the live coordinator seat (is_coordinator:true, no role string) and on every role seat's first-ever SessionStart (role gets stamped by a separate registration step that runs AFTER this hook). Skip entirely (no signal, no DB call) when existingMetadata is null/undefined or the verdict is 'unknown'. On a definitive 'role' or 'worker' verdict: compute the expected model via model-policy.cjs's policyModelFor(verdict); compare the observed model via model-policy.cjs's OWN coarseModelAlias (not the hook-local coarseModelAlias, which passes an unrecognized id through unchanged and would false-positive -- model-policy's returns null for an unrecognized id). On a mismatch, call emit() (real emitFeedback in production) which performs its own day-salted dedup_hash insert-or-noop -- never an UPDATE-based dedup, since public.feedback's append-only trigger (confirmed live) rejects every UPDATE outright. Call signalModelPolicyMismatch as the LAST statement inside main(), strictly after upsertSessionRow() and the tick-daemon spawn block, wrapped in its own try/catch so a throw anywhere inside it can never block, delay, or fail the existing env-file write, identity markers, /current pointer, claude_sessions upsert, or tick-daemon spawn. Honor a new LEO_MODEL_POLICY_SIGNAL=0 kill switch (checked first, before any other work in the function); the hook's existing LEO_HOOK_DRY_RUN=1 early-return already occurs before this insertion point, so dry-run mode requires no additional guarding.
acceptance_criteria: A session with no pre-existing claude_sessions row (existingMetadata null/undefined) never signals, regardless of the observed model -- fixes the measured false-positive on every role seat's first-ever SessionStart.

existingMetadata with no role key, no is_coordinator, and no non_fleet flag classifies as 'worker'; existingMetadata with is_coordinator:true, non_fleet:true, or a recognized role string classifies as 'role' -- classification is delegated entirely to role-status-identity.cjs's verdictFromMetadata, never re-implemented.

A worker-classified session observed running any Fable-family model id signals exactly once per day; an identical second SessionStart the same day inserts zero additional feedback rows (emitFeedback's built-in dedup, verified via injected emit spy or a real DB round-trip in an integration test).
A role-classified session observed running its policy model (claude-fable-5-1 alias) never signals.
Forcing the injected emit (or supabase call) to throw does not prevent main() from completing and calling resolve() -- proves session registration is unaffected by a bug in the new code.
LEO_MODEL_POLICY_SIGNAL=0 suppresses the entire check (asserted via an injected emit spy never being invoked, and no supabase call being made).

functional_requirements.title: Fleet-dashboard "seats off policy" count
functional_requirements.description: In scripts/fleet-dashboard.cjs, at the existing per-session metadata projection (already selects the full metadata JSONB blob -- no new query, no new column), classify each session using the SAME two modules as FR-1 (role-status-identity.cjs's verdictFromMetadata, already-in-hand metadata, purely synchronous; model-policy.cjs's policyModelFor/coarseModelAlias) and add one summary line reporting the count of sessions currently off their seat-class policy. This item has no dependency on FR-1 and may ship in its own commit, before or after FR-1. On any degraded input (a malformed metadata row, or the classification modules failing to load), the line MUST abstain (e.g. render 'N/A' or omit the line) rather than silently render a false '0 seats off policy' -- an abstained count must never be mistaken for a clean bill of health.
acceptance_criteria: Given a fixture set of session rows including a coordinator-shaped row (is_coordinator:true, no role string), a genuine worker-on-Fable row, and a role-seat-on-its-policy-model row, the computed off-policy count matches the hand-computed expected count exactly (1, from the worker-on-Fable row only -- the coordinator-shaped row must NOT be miscounted as off-policy).
The dashboard issues no additional Supabase query beyond what it already runs to build the session list.
A simulated classification failure (e.g. an unparseable/non-object metadata value on one row) causes the summary line to abstain, never to render 0.

functional_requirements.title: Fail-open safety, and CI-visible test coverage
functional_requirements.description: The FR-1 mismatch-signal path must be provably incapable of degrading existing SessionStart behavior, and the new tests for FR-1/FR-2 must be genuinely exercised by CI, not merely present on disk. Prospective testing-agent evidence measured that vitest's CI config (hooks-harness-tests.yml) only collects *.test.js files in tests/unit/hooks/ -- the three existing *.test.cjs suites in that directory are dark (never collected, confirmed via `npx vitest list`) -- so new tests MUST be authored as new *.test.js files, following the tests/unit/hooks/session-role-orient-adam-branch.test.js placement precedent, never appended to an existing *.test.cjs file. Because emitFeedback (ESM, lib/governance/emit-feedback.js) is invoked from a CommonJS hook, the require() call itself must live inside the SAME fail-open try/catch as the rest of signalModelPolicyMismatch, so an ESM/CJS interop failure on any given Node runtime degrades silently to "no signal" rather than a hook crash -- this was measured to work on the authoring machine's node v24.12.0, but CI's runner Node version must be independently confirmed, not assumed identical.
acceptance_criteria: New FR-1 and FR-2 test files are named *.test.js (never *.test.cjs) and are confirmed collected by `npx vitest list` before being relied upon as CI-enforced coverage.
The exact vitest invocation hooks-harness-tests.yml runs in CI is reproduced locally and confirmed to include the new test file(s) in its collected set.
A CI-runtime check (not merely a local one) confirms require()-ing lib/governance/emit-feedback.js from the CJS hook context does not throw ERR_REQUIRE_ESM on the CI runner's actual Node version.

technical_requirements.title: No schema change
technical_requirements.description: All new signals persist through the existing feedback table (INSERT only, compatible with its live append-only trigger) and the existing claude_sessions.metadata JSONB column; fleet-dashboard.cjs consumes only already-selected columns. No migration, no new table, no new column.

technical_requirements.title: Zero behavior change to existing SessionStart registration
technical_requirements.description: The env-file write, identity markers, /current pointer, claude_sessions upsert, and tick-daemon spawn in scripts/hooks/capture-session-id.cjs are untouched. The new code is strictly additive, appended after all of it, and isolated in its own try/catch so it cannot affect any of the above even if it throws.

technical_requirements.title: Single source of truth for classification and policy
technical_requirements.description: lib/fleet/role-status-identity.cjs's verdictFromMetadata/roleVerdictFor is the ONLY role classifier used by FR-1 and FR-2; lib/fleet/model-policy.cjs's policyModelFor/coarseModelAlias is the ONLY policy/alias logic used. No duplicate or parallel classification logic is introduced in the hook or the dashboard.

test_scenarios.expected: No signal (existingMetadata is null/undefined, skipped before classification)

test_scenarios.scenario: Coordinator-shaped existingMetadata (is_coordinator:true, no role string), observed running claude-fable-5-1
test_scenarios.expected: Classified 'role' via verdictFromMetadata, no mismatch (Fable IS the role policy model) -- proves the coordinator false-positive from the naive approach is fixed

test_scenarios.scenario: Worker existingMetadata (no role/is_coordinator/non_fleet), observed running claude-fable-5-1
test_scenarios.expected: Signals exactly once via injected emit spy; a second identical call the same day does not double-insert
main() still completes and calls resolve(); no unhandled rejection
emit spy never called, no supabase call made

test_scenarios.scenario: fleet-dashboard.cjs fixture: coordinator-shaped row + worker-on-Fable row + role-on-policy row
fleet-dashboard.cjs fixture with one malformed metadata row

test_scenarios.expected: `npx vitest list` includes the new *.test.js file(s); running hooks-harness-tests.yml's exact vitest invocation locally reproduces the same collected set

acceptance_criteria: FR-1's signal fires only on a definitive role/worker classification derived from the hook's pre-write metadata snapshot, never on an unknown/absent-row case -- the measured false positive on the coordinator seat and on every role seat's first SessionStart is eliminated.
FR-1 is fail-open: no code path inside signalModelPolicyMismatch can block, delay, or fail existing SessionStart registration.
FR-2 ships independently of FR-1, needs no new DB query, and abstains rather than falsely reporting a clean bill of health on a degraded read.
All new tests are in *.test.js files confirmed collected by the CI vitest invocation -- not silently dark *.test.cjs files.

risks.risk: A role seat's very first SessionStart (before any role-registration step has run) still classifies as 'worker' and could false-positive once per chairman restart cycle.
risks.mitigation: Accepted as a one-time, self-healing edge case: the NEXT SessionStart for that same seat reads existingMetadata AFTER the role-registration write completed, and classifies correctly. Documented explicitly rather than engineered away, since eliminating it entirely would require a second DB round-trip inside the hook's tight timeout budget.

risks.risk: The feedback table (append-only, no cleanup) accumulates one row per genuine daily mismatch indefinitely.
risks.mitigation: emitFeedback's built-in day-salted dedup already bounds this to at most one row per seat per day per mismatch; a genuinely off-policy seat is expected to be fixed promptly (restart under the correct --model), not left running for weeks.

risks.risk: require()-ing an ESM module (lib/governance/emit-feedback.js) from a CJS hook may throw ERR_REQUIRE_ESM on a Node version other than the one manually verified.
risks.mitigation: The require() call is wrapped in the same fail-open try/catch as the rest of the signal logic, degrading to 'no signal' rather than a hook crash; FR-3's acceptance criteria require an explicit CI-runtime confirmation, not an assumption carried over from local testing.

risks.risk: New tests silently never run in CI if placed in a *.test.cjs file, exactly as measured for the three pre-existing dark suites in tests/unit/hooks/.
risks.mitigation: FR-3 requires new tests be *.test.js files and requires an explicit `npx vitest list` collection check before relying on them.

consumers: Chairman-facing feedback inbox (reads new mismatch-signal rows)
Fleet-dashboard viewers (read the new off-policy count line via npm run fleet:dashboard)
data_contracts: none -- no schema change; feedback and claude_sessions column shapes are unchanged
runtime_config: LEO_MODEL_POLICY_SIGNAL (new kill switch, default enabled; set to 0 to disable FR-1 entirely)
LEO_HOOK_DRY_RUN (pre-existing, already short-circuits before the new insertion point)
observability_rollout: New feedback rows are visible immediately in the existing chairman feedback inbox/query surfaces
The new fleet-dashboard summary line is visible on every dashboard run with no rollout gating needed

system_architecture.summary: Two independent, additive signals built entirely on two pre-existing pure classifier modules (role-status-identity.cjs, model-policy.cjs) -- no new module, no schema change, no new table.

implementation_approach.summary: Ship FR-1 and FR-2 as two separate, independently revertible commits; FR-2 has no dependency on FR-1 and may land first or separately.
steps: Re-verify against current main (not this PRD's authoring-time snapshot) that capture-session-id.cjs's main() still fetches existingMetadata before its upsert, at the exact point buildSessionMetadata(existingMetadata, ...) is called.
Implement signalModelPolicyMismatch() with injected deps (supabase, emit, now), exported for testing; wire the single fail-open call at the tail of main().
Add a new tests/unit/hooks/*.test.js file covering all FR-1 acceptance criteria; confirm via `npx vitest list` it is collected.
Implement the fleet-dashboard.cjs off-policy line; add its own new *.test.js file covering FR-2 acceptance criteria.
Reproduce hooks-harness-tests.yml's exact vitest invocation locally to confirm CI parity for both new test files.
Commit FR-1 and FR-2 separately; open PR(s) accordingly.
